passage.title: Culture shock
passage.html:
affects  ·  although  ·  as a result  ·  effects  ·  especially  ·  in fact  ·  on the other hand  ·  percent  ·  percentage  ·  problem  ·  so  ·  therefore  ·  trouble

We may think that different parts of the world are becoming more and more similar, but culture shock is still a very common (1) …… for people who travel to another country. It (2) …… most travellers by making them anxious, homesick or uncomfortable in the new culture. (3) …… most people eventually grow accustomed to the new country, the (4) …… of culture shock can last for years.

It is likely that a lower (5) …… of tourists suffer from culture shock than people going to work or study in a new country. Tourists tend to spend time with other tourists and stay in international hotels. (6) ……, they do not live with the local population or have to cope with the culture.

Culture shock is (7) …… strong for people going to work abroad. On the one hand, they have to deal with a difficult new working environment and (8) …… they do not get the support which students or other overseas visitors receive. (9) ……, nearly 30 (10) …… of overseas workers and their families find culture shock so hard to cope with that they return home early.

passage.title: City life and health
passage.html:
Many aspects of city life, such as pollution, may be harmful (harm) to our health and general well-being and most people find living and working in big cities (11) …… (stress). They are (12) …… (general) in such a hurry that they do not eat well. Also, their exercise routine tends to be (13) …… (regular) and there may be many days or weeks when they take no exercise at all.

However, studies show that it is extremely important to be (14) …… (care) about what you eat. A (15) …… (health) diet should include plenty of fresh fruit and vegetables. On the other hand, you can put on weight (16) …… (ease) if you eat well but do not take exercise, so it is important to take a (17) …… (reason) amount of exercise every day to stay fit. Unfortunately, our routines often make it (18) …… (convenient) or difficult to find time for regular exercise. When people start to take exercise, their feeling of well-being often increases (19) …… (dramatic) and they also benefit from an increased level of (20) …… (fit).

parts.label: Part 3
parts.name: Adjectives and adverbs
parts.rubric: Questions 21 – 30 · Complete the sentences with the correct form of the adjective or adverb in brackets.

qs.text: If you study in the country where the language is spoken, you will learn to speak it (well) than if you stay at home.
My diet has improved because I eat (little) than I did in the past.
In my experience, rich people are not always (happy) than poor people.
Taking exercise outdoors is (enjoyable) than going to a gym.
They gave the prize to Saleem because he was the student in the class who had worked the (hard).
People won't understand you unless you speak (clearly) than you do now.
The distance from London to Bangkok is (far) than the distance to Moscow.
Pollution in my country is growing (bad), because nowadays there is more traffic and more industry.
In Australia, January is often the (hot) month of the year.
Brisbane had the second (high) rainfall in its history this year.
